title: Audit scale-dependent seed averaging in the full recurrence
body:
Scale-dependent seed switching was proposed as a way to improve recursive cost using a log-scale average of seed exponents. This package gives an exact counterexample to that unconditional substitution in the stated positive recurrence: two complete profiles with roots 1/4 and 3/4 yield p_eff=log_256(19+3 sqrt(33)) in (5/8,2/3), rather than 1/2. The predecessor's explicit oscillation-error bound permits the discrepancy; a sublinear error estimate is needed before dropping it.

A separate positive-tree comparison proves that arbitrary per-node switching cannot beat the best fixed seed in a finite positive catalogue with zero glue, bounded child ratios and unit terminal cost. That limited extremal conclusion survives independently of root averaging. Both child ranks, all multiplicities and terminal overshoot are retained; a unit additive toll leaves the counterexample exponent unchanged. No physical seed, supplier admission, outer transfer or new kappa is claimed.

Validation: registered CPython 3.12.12 replay with `-I -O -B`; a separate mathematical worker's exact rank-history implementation (1,023 schedules and 112,311 total rank histories); 11 semantic controls across the two implementations; exact committed-byte preflight; Git-free read-only CPython 3.14.6 replay. These support written all-scale proofs, not formal-kernel or independent human review. No selected cold replay was needed or performed; selected binding check passes.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/scale-dependent-seed-moment-audit
```
